entwurf.beschreibung: A concise video tracing Harley‑Davidson from its 1903 Milwaukee shed beginnings through wartime production, global expansion, and modern offerings.

teile.name: Opening
teile.text: Harley‑Davidson started in 1903 in a Milwaukee shed.
teile.szene: A painted urban poster shows a dimly lit wooden shed in 1903 Milwaukee, two young men hunched over a metal frame, daylight filtering through a small window.

teile.name: Engine Upgrade
teile.text: In 1904 their 405‑cc loop‑frame prototype raced, finishing fourth.
teile.szene: A stylized poster depicts a 1904 Harley on a racetrack, the rider leaning forward, the engine exposed, crowd cheering under early‑morning light.

teile.name: Police Contracts
teile.text: By 1907 production rose to 150 bikes, and police adopted them.
teile.szene: An illustrated city street in 1907, a police officer rides a freshly polished Harley past brick storefronts, sunlight glinting off chrome.

teile.name: WWI Contribution
teile.text: World War I spurred orders; 20,000 motorcycles sold to the U.S. military.
teile.szene: A wartime poster shows a convoy of Harleys crossing a dusty trench road, soldiers in uniform riding side by side under a smoky sky.

teile.name: Global Factories
teile.text: Since then the company expanded, building factories in the U.S., Brazil, Thailand.
teile.szene: A vibrant poster collage shows two modern plants: one with tropical foliage in Brazil, another with sleek steel lines in Thailand, sunrise lighting each.

teile.name: Modern Lineup
teile.text: The original shed moved to Juneau Avenue, standing as a tribute.
teile.szene: A contemporary urban poster shows a rider on a chrome‑finished custom cruiser beside a sleek VRSC, neon city backdrop, night lights reflecting off metal.

teile.name: Call To Action
teile.text: If you enjoyed this history, like, share, and save.
teile.szene: The presenter, drawn in the same poster style, points toward a stylized button, smiling, with bold lettering inviting interaction.
